query: For additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs degradation during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases and why catastrophic failure may occur? Specify a controlled change that would reveal the governing behavior, predicted observations relative to the starting-state baseline, applicable exposure boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: In laser–powder-bed–fused Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 with an fcc matrix, elevated-temperature environmental degradation is governed by the percolating AM segregation network (Al/Ti-enriched interdendritic/GB regions and Cr-depleted boundaries) that controls both oxide-scale stability and oxygen ingress. In oxidizing gases containing water vapor, chromia formed on Cr-rich areas is destabilized by Cr oxyhydroxide volatilization, causing rapid local Cr depletion and a transition to non-protective spinel/Fe–Co–Ni oxides while promoting internal oxidation of Al/Ti along the segregated network. In sufficiently reducing gases (low pO2), protective chromia cannot nucleate, and the same network accelerates deep internal oxidation of Al/Ti. Catastrophic failure occurs when this internally oxidized, brittle, percolating network undergoes stress-assisted intergranular cracking and crack coalescence.
generation.material_initial_state: As-built laser PBF Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 with an fcc matrix; cellular/interdendritic substructure, Al/Ti-enriched interdendritic/B2–Laves particles, Cr-depleted grain boundaries; residual tensile stresses; surface polished to 1 μm finish prior to exposure.
generation.intervention: Homogenization/solution treatment to disrupt the percolating segregation network: 1100 °C for 2 h in high-purity Ar, followed by water quench, yielding reduced Al/Ti partitioning, dissolution of interdendritic B2/Laves, and more uniform Cr distribution (grain size kept comparable by limiting hold time).
generation.conditions: Isothermal exposure at 800 °C for 10 h under three controlled atmospheres at 1 atm total pressure and 50 sccm cm−2 flow: (i) dry O2 (pH2O < 1e−4 atm), (ii) wet O2 (pH2O ≈ 0.1 atm), (iii) H2/H2O mixture setting pO2 ≈ 1e−20 atm (via humidified H2 at known dew point). Identical thermal histories for as-built vs homogenized specimens.
generation.structural_mediator: Percolating interdendritic/GB network consisting of Al/Ti-rich B2/Laves particles and Cr-depleted boundaries that act as preferential diffusion/oxidation paths and crack paths.
generation.mechanism: Supply-limited protective scale behavior governed by local Cr activity and water-vapor-driven chromia volatilization: (a) In wet oxidizing gas, Cr2O3 is consumed as volatile Cr oxyhydroxides, depleting Cr near the surface along segregated paths and forcing transition to non-protective oxides/spinels; concurrent internal oxidation of Al/Ti embrittles the network. (b) In low-pO2 reducing gas, chromia cannot form; oxygen at very low chemical potential promotes deep internal oxidation of Al/Ti along the same network. Thermal/oxidation stresses then drive stress-assisted intergranular cracking along the internally oxidized, brittle network, causing catastrophic failure.
generation.predicted_outcome:
- Relative to the as-built baseline in dry O2: Homogenized samples exhibit lower oxidation kinetics and improved scale adherence in all atmospheres. Quantitatively, mass-gain rate constants decrease by roughly 2–5× in dry and wet O2 and internal oxidation depths are reduced by ~30–60% at 800 °C. 
- Wet O2 vs dry O2 (as-built): Early breakaway in wet O2 (onset time reduced by ~3–10×), an order-of-magnitude increase in instantaneous mass-gain rate after breakaway, and dense intergranular crack networks coincident with segregated paths; catastrophic cracking upon cooling or during bend testing is likely. 
- Reducing H2/H2O (pO2 ≈ 1e−20 atm): No continuous external chromia; instead, a deep internal oxidation front with fine Al/Ti oxides forms. As-built shows deeper internal oxidation (e.g., >10–30 μm after 10 h) and greater near-surface hardening/embrittlement than homogenized; homogenized shows shallower fronts and higher retained ductility at temperature.
generation.baseline: As-built material exposed at 800 °C for 10 h in dry O2 forms a mostly adherent chromia/spinel scale with parabolic-like mass gain, limited internal oxidation (few μm) and few surface/GB cracks; bend ductility at temperature remains measurable without catastrophic failure.
generation.boundary: Applicable for 700–950 °C exposures. In oxidizing gases with pH2O ≥ ~0.01 atm, chromia volatilization becomes significant and promotes breakaway; below this pH2O and at moderate pO2, protective behavior is more likely. In reducing gases with effective pO2 ≤ ~1e−18–1e−20 atm at 700–900 °C, protective chromia is not sustained and internal oxidation dominates. The hypothesis assumes Al ~3–5 at% and Ti ~5–7 at% with insufficient Al to form continuous external alumina.
generation.uncertainty: Exact identity and volume fraction of interdendritic phases (B2 vs Laves) and their dissolution kinetics; grain growth during homogenization; precise critical pH2O/pO2 thresholds for chromia volatilization and breakaway at this composition; role of applied/mechanical stresses vs intrinsic oxidation stresses; potential hydrogen effects in reducing atmospheres; quantitative factors (rate constants, depths) may vary with powder chemistry and AM build parameters.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare matched as-built and homogenized coupons. Expose at 800 °C for 10 h under dry O2, wet O2 (pH2O ≈ 0.1 atm), and H2/H2O (pO2 ≈ 1e−20 atm). Track mass change continuously (TGA) and acoustic emission for cracking. After exposure, perform cross-sectional SEM/EDS mapping to quantify scale type/thickness and internal oxidation depth; EPMA/SIMS line scans for Cr depletion; XRD for oxide phases; nanoindentation/microhardness profiles vs depth; in-situ 4-point bend or ring compression at 800 °C to assess embrittlement; correlate crack paths with prior segregated network (EBSD + EDS).
measurements: Mass gain vs time (to detect parabolic vs breakaway kinetics)
Acoustic emission event rate during exposure/cool-down (cracking)
Oxide scale phase ID (XRD/Raman) and thickness (SEM cross-sections)
Internal oxidation depth and Al/Ti-oxide dispersion (SEM/EDS, TEM if needed)
Crack density and path relative to prior interdendritic/GB network (EBSD/EDS mapping)
High-temperature bend/creep ductility comparison (as-built vs homogenized)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if one or more occur: (i) Homogenization does not reduce oxidation kinetics, internal oxidation depth, or crack density relative to as-built in any atmosphere; (ii) Increasing pH2O from <1e−4 to ~0.1 atm does not accelerate transition from protective to non-protective behavior nor increase Cr depletion; (iii) Catastrophic cracking does not localize along the prior segregated/GB network or occurs without evidence of internal Al/Ti oxidation and Cr depletion; (iv) In low-pO2 reducing gas, a continuous, protective chromia scale forms and internal oxidation is negligible.
